high.title: People Rush to Deposit Money in Banks
high.summary: Vietnamese banks are experiencing an intense deposit mobilization race in March 2026, with widespread interest rate increases establishing a new high plateau. Some banks have reached 9%/year. Techcombank launched programs offering additional 1%/year for new deposits in March 2026, bringing rates up to 8.4%/year for 3-12 month terms. The bank also raised its rate sheet from March 27, pushing 12-month rates to 7.4%/year maximum. Sacombank offers preferential rates for new counter deposits from March 26 to June 30. This deposit rate war indicates banks are competing aggressively for funding amid liquidity pressures, which could impact lending margins and banking sector profitability. For VND traders, this suggests potential pressure on the currency as banks seek to attract deposits to manage funding costs.

high.title: State Bank of Vietnam Requires Stabilization of Interest Rate Levels
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) issued a directive requiring credit institutions and foreign bank branches to focus on stabilizing market interest rate levels. The SBV demands strict implementation of Directive 01/CT-NHNN dated January 9, 2026, regarding key banking tasks to maintain macroeconomic stability, control inflation, and support sustainable economic growth. Banks must implement solutions to stabilize interest rate levels, strictly comply with SBV interest rate regulations (deposit rate quotations, maximum deposit rates), strengthen internal control and inspection, and handle violations promptly. This intervention comes amid the recent deposit rate war and reflects the central bank's concern about rising funding costs potentially destabilizing the monetary policy transmission mechanism. For bond investors and FX traders, this signals the SBV's commitment to containing rate volatility that could impact VND stability.

medium.title: Banking Industry Outlook 2026: Adapting to Liquidity Pressure and New Structural Phase
medium.summary: Dragon Capital (VDSC) analysis shows Vietnamese banking is entering a new structural phase with ambitious 10% GDP growth targets but limited monetary policy easing room. Growth momentum is shifting toward fiscal policy and capital markets for long-term investment funding. Banks face cyclical liquidity pressures driving interest rate increases since late 2025. Credit growth reached only 1.44% through February 2026 while deposit growth remains constrained, creating funding mismatches that pressure net interest margins.

medium.title: One Bank Prepares to Implement 20% Stock Dividend
medium.summary: Nam A Bank's Board of Directors approved a capital increase plan for 2026, raising charter capital from over VND 17.156 trillion to over VND 22.588 trillion through three stock issuance methods. The plan includes issuing 343 million shares (20% ratio) from retained earnings and reserve funds, 100 million ESOP shares, and private placement shares. This capital expansion reflects banking sector growth ambitions amid the new regulatory environment.

medium.title: VN-Index Falls 110 Points Since Beginning of Year: Focus on Vingroup, Vietjet, FPT
medium.summary: Vietnam's stock market ended Q1 2026 turbulently despite strong early performance when VN-Index first exceeded 1,900. The index lost over 200 points in March alone (nearly 11% decline), totaling 110 points lost from year-start. Clear divergence emerged between state-controlled and private conglomerate stocks, with Vingroup companies (VIC, VHM, VPL, VRE) alone causing nearly 60 points of VN-Index decline since early 2026, reflecting profit-taking after strong 2025 gains.

medium.title: From Tomorrow, Vietcombank, VietinBank, Agribank... Stop All Money Transfer/Receipt Transactions for Following Case
medium.summary: From April 1, 2026, per SBV Circular 30/2025 on non-cash payment services, commercial banks must ensure all payment account names match Citizen Identity Card information exactly. This ends nickname/iNick services that allowed users to use custom names instead of account numbers for transactions, reducing transfer errors but making transactions less convenient.
